rationale: Pins #994: enumerators declared inside a preprocessor arm of an enumerator list are real members. Found by the D4 jq differential draw — jq/src/jv_dtoa.c:1630-1643 declares `enum { #ifdef IEEE_Arith emax = ...; emin = ... #else emin = ...` inside a function whose whole file the parser wraps in one ERROR; the analyzer's enum loop read only DIRECT children of enumerator_list, saw the preproc_ifdef node, and published no member, so the differential read 2 MISSING rows (contains -> emax, contains -> emin). The rule added is the STRUCT-field rule the analyzer already applies to conditional members: a preprocessor arm is the same declaration under a condition. The fixture is function-local because that is the parse shape the corpus has (the same text at file scope recovers as an ERROR child instead, a different shape).

expectRelationships.comment: CONTROL: an ordinary enumerator BEFORE the arm. A fix that replaced the loop instead of recursing would lose it.
THE PINNED MEMBER from the true region of the #ifdef.
THE PINNED MEMBER; declared in BOTH arms, so two occurrences are expected (see the count row).

expectRelationshipCount.note: unguarded_first + emax + emin(#ifdef arm) + emin(#else arm). The duplicate emin is intentional: both arms are declarations in the file, and the count pins that the recursion publishes the arm members rather than one merged row.
